# Run

The graphs in `out/` are written for the AMT runner. This page says what has been checked and how
to run the check yourself.

## Checked in this repository

`python main.py` runs the tests in `tests/test_convert.py` after every build. They check that:

- the weights of every stone add up to 1 (tolerance of rounding);
- every statement has exactly one weight, one method and one piece of evidence, and at most one type;
- the evidence string equals the label of the reading;
- no statement is a blank node, and two conversions give identical Turtle;
- the type follows the rule: c < 1 vagueness, a < 1 uncertainty, both fuzziness-wobbliness, neither none.

The SHACL shapes of the AMT engine are not part of the default build, because they live in the engine
repository. The runner applies them in the next step.

## Check with the AMT runner

The check needs network access, because the runner fetches the engine from GitHub. It is therefore its own
step and is not part of the default build:

```
python main.py --only check
```

It clones the [amt-runner](https://github.com/alpaca-fair-framework/amt-runner) into `build/` (ignored by git), then calls
`run_amt.py <graph> --check-only --update` for each of the seven graphs. `--check-only` validates against the
AMT shapes, loads the graph and runs the diagnostics (`AMT-E101`, `AMT-E102`, `AMT-E103`, `AMT-N301`), and
writes no output. The report is `build/check-report.txt`.

## What the engine does with these graphs

The graphs contain **no axioms** (no role chains, inverses or subsumptions). A full run of the runner
therefore validates and exports, but infers nothing. Axioms are a modelling decision, not a technicality. The
proposals are in the PRIMER, steps S3 to S5.

## Questions for review

1. Is the confidence of a historical reading read from editor-marked characters (`[ ] ( ) ? / \ - . :`) a fair
   proxy for reading confidence?
2. Is string similarity of 0.60 a sensible threshold for "the same reading"? Two editors who differ in one
   letter of eight read alike; two who differ in three do not.
3. Should a stone with a single, unmarked reading carry a type at all? Currently it carries none.
4. The weights are shares among alternatives (sum 1). Is that the right reading of "weight" for a single,
   damaged reading, given that the damage then shows in the type and not in the number? (See
   [Weights](weights.html).)
